transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. I came in because, honestly, for a long time now I’ve just been walking around with this flat, heavy feeling. Even when work is going fine or people are nice to me, I still feel... down, I guess. Just kind of empty most days. So I figured it was time to talk to someone about it.
When you say 'for a long time now' — are we talking weeks, months, or has this flat, heavy feeling been going on for years?

It's been years, actually. I'd say... about two years and two months now. It pretty much started right around the time this big dashboard project put me in the spotlight at work, and it just hasn't really gone away since then.

Over these past two years, has your mood been consistently low and flat the whole time, or have there been periods where you felt noticeably better — even if just for a few weeks — before the heaviness came back?

I don't really remember any times where it went away, to be honest. It's just been this constant... low baseline. Like, maybe a day here or there where I'm a little distracted, but definitely not weeks at a time where I felt better. It's just always there.

During these two years, have there been any stretches of time — even a few days or a week — where you felt unusually energetic, more talkative than usual, needed less sleep, or had racing thoughts or lots of ideas?
No, not at all. I haven't really had any days like that. If anything, I'm usually just tired. I definitely haven't felt unusually energetic or had racing thoughts or anything like that.

Before these past two years, did you ever have a period — even if it was just a few days — where you felt unusually high or euphoric, had a lot more energy than normal, or felt like you could do anything and didn't need much sleep?

No, nothing like that ever. I've never had a time where I felt super high or energetic, or like I didn't need sleep. Even before all this started two years ago, I was just... normal, I guess. Never anything extreme like what you're describing.
In those two years, have there been any weeks or longer stretches where your mood lifted back to what felt like your normal baseline before all this started, even if it didn't last very long?

No, honestly, I don't think so. It's just been pretty much the same the whole time. I haven't really had a week or anything where I felt like my old normal. It's just been this... constant low feeling for the whole two years.
Over these two years, have there been any periods of a couple of months or longer where your mood was noticeably better than it is now — even if you still wouldn't call it 'good' or 'normal'?

No, not really. It hasn't ever let up for that long. Like I said, it's just been pretty much constant for the whole two years. I haven't had any breaks where things felt noticeably better for a couple of months.

Have you ever had a period in your life — even before these past two years — where you felt noticeably happier, more confident, or more productive than your usual self, even if people around you thought you were acting a bit different or 'too much'?
No, I really haven't. I've never had a time where I felt unusually happy or super productive, or where people thought I was acting weird or 'too much.' It's just never happened.

During these two years of feeling low, have there been any periods — even just a few days — where you felt noticeably more confident, more motivated to do things, or took on more projects or responsibilities than you normally would, even if you wouldn't call it 'high' or 'energetic'?
No, I haven't. I haven't had any days where I felt more motivated or took on extra projects or anything like that. It's really just been the same low feeling the whole time.

During these two years, have there been any stretches of several weeks where your mood was somewhat lighter or you felt a bit more like yourself — not back to normal, but noticeably better than the heaviness you're describing now?
No, not even for a few weeks. I know I keep saying the same thing, but it really has just been... heavy, the entire time. I haven't had any stretches where it lifted or I felt more like my old self.

I want to ask about something a bit different. Have you ever had a time in your life — even just a few days — where you felt noticeably more optimistic, took on new projects or goals with enthusiasm, or felt like things were actually possible, even if people around you didn't think you were acting unusual?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I don't think I've ever felt that kind of optimism or enthusiasm for anything in a long time. It's just... I haven't had any days like that where I felt like things were suddenly possible or where I wanted to take on new goals. It's just been flat and low.
Have there been any times — even just a few days in a row — where you needed significantly less sleep than usual but still felt rested, or where you slept much less but didn't feel tired?

No, honestly, I've always needed my sleep. If I don't get enough, I definitely feel it the next day. I haven't had any times where I just didn't need to sleep or felt fine on less rest. It's usually the opposite, honestly.
Have you ever had a period — even just a few days — where your mood was elevated or you felt unusually good or happy, separate from just not feeling depressed?

No, I haven't. I don't think I've ever felt unusually good or elevated like that. It's really just been... well, just this low feeling for as long as I can remember. I haven't had any days where I felt super happy or anything out of the ordinary.

I know you've said you haven't felt unusually energetic or happy, but I want to ask specifically: have you ever had a period — even just a few days — where you were doing a lot more than usual, felt like you were accomplishing things, and didn't feel tired even though you were doing more, even if people didn't think you were acting strange?

No, I really haven't. Um, if I try to take on extra things or do more than my normal routine, I definitely feel it. I've never had a stretch of days where I was just getting a bunch of stuff done and not feeling exhausted by it. It's usually a struggle just to get through my regular work, so... no, nothing like what you're describing.

Have you ever had a period where you slept significantly less than usual — like 3-4 hours instead of your normal 7-8 — but felt energized or well-rested despite the reduced sleep, even if just for a day or two?

No, I think that's kind of like what you asked earlier... but no, never. If I only get three or four hours of sleep, I'm completely dead on my feet the next day. I've never felt energized or well-rested on that little sleep, not even for just one day.

I want to be very specific here: have you ever had a stretch of 4 or more days in a row where you needed noticeably less sleep than usual — like sleeping 5 hours instead of your normal 8 — and during those days you felt okay or even good, not exhausted?
No, I haven't. Um, like I said, if I don't get enough sleep, I feel it. I definitely don't feel okay or good on less sleep, even if it was just for a few days. I just feel tired.

Have you ever had a stretch of 4 or more days where you felt noticeably happier, more cheerful, or in a better mood than your baseline — not necessarily 'high' or 'euphoric,' just genuinely better — even if it only happened once?

No, I haven't. Honestly, I can't really remember the last time I felt genuinely cheerful or in a noticeably better mood for that long. It's pretty much just been this same kind of low feeling for a while now. So, no, I haven't had a stretch like that.
